newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise in sluggish trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise in sluggish trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Monday in thin and trendless trading, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 0.37 percent, or 0.90 points, to 246.81 on a very low all-share turnover of 93 million shekels against 137 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.49 percent higher at 255.62.

"Trading was trendless and the market is looking for direction. Investors are waiting for further developments on the political front," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House, referring to Israel's plan for more Jewish housing in East Jerusalem and a police probe of alleged government corruption.

"The market was very quiet today and investors are waiting to see what will happen on Wall Street. The market is very stable but it is hard to predict where is it going," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.
"The outlook for the market is still positive but in the near term it is expected to stabilise at the current level," Weisberg added.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 1.5 percent to 20,322 agorot on volume of 4.5 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which rose 1.0 percent to 627 on turnover of 3.6 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which gained 0.75 percent to end at 31,225 agorot on turnover of 3.2 million shekels.
